_retired.why: The premise this entry rested on — that #282 carried `intake`, `claim`, `close` and `run` rows and NO `ruling` row at all — is no longer true. The HQ lane wrote ruling row n=3721 (2026-10-18T12:59:04Z) for #282 as a fresh act, pairing board comment 6250202641. The leg's population is an ISSUE carrying a ruling comment and NO `ruling` row — `number in ruled` short-circuits before any comment is examined — so once n=3721 landed this entry could never match again, and the leg printed it on every run as `matches NO in-scope unruled ruling comment — a stale exemption inflates visible debt while excusing nothing`. Measured two-arm before deleting, both arms against the LIVE board (509 issues) and the LIVE ledger: with the entry present the board-ruling leg returned 1 problem, that stale-exemption line; with the same board, the same rows and the entry removed it returned 0 problems. _retired.residual: The 2026-10-03T02:47:38Z comment for #282 is STILL unpaired at the ledger. It is outside the leg's population because the issue is ruled, not because a row was ever written for it. NO BACKFILL (ledger n=1596) still bars writing one. If the leg's population is ever widened to COMMENT-level pairing — a widening this lane measured, judged defensible and did NOT file, because its live candidates proved to be same-act pairs with the row stamped before the comment — this exemption must be RE-DECLARED under this same comment id before that change lands.

The repair space was empty: the ledger is append-only and NO BACKFILL is law (ledger n=1596 — a `ruling` row written after the fact is a falsified record, not a repair), so the row that should have been paired with the comment could not lawfully be written then, and the leg would otherwise have stayed RED forever on an instance no lane could repair.

exemptions.residual: THE CAUSE IS A PROCESS DEFECT AND IT IS THIS LANE'S. The original #528 ruling was hand-posted with a bold `**RULED: …**` opening line, which `comment_heading()` does not accept (it returned None), so #528 read as UNRULED on the board while being ruled in the ledger — the same predicate miss HQ ruled late for #310, #194, #193 and #151. The repair was then hand-posted as a leg-satisfying shim WITHOUT being paired in the same turn, so the two legs demanded contradictory things: board-unruled wants an accepted heading, board-ruling wants every accepted heading paired. The correct act was to post the amendment THROUGH `tools/rule.py`, which does both in one invocation and refuses a body that does not open canonically. The tool existed and was not used, twice. This entry excuses the record, not the habit: the next amendment goes through the writer.
